cleanIntro: Henry's .30/30 book, which covers the H009 and H009B. This is an older and differently written manual from the rest of the Henry set, and it is the only one that publishes a real lever-action takedown — lever screw, lever, bolt, then the ejector. Read the bore-direction note: this book differs from Henry's newer manuals and the guide follows THIS book.

steps.title: Transfer bar, and what it means for carrying
steps.action: This rifle uses a patented transfer-bar safety: it can fire only with the hammer fully cocked and the trigger pulled, so it is meant to be carried with the hammer fully down. There is no half-cock notch and no crossbolt. Do not go hunting for the .22 Henry's 1/4-cock Safety position — this action does not have one.
steps.aside: Please note that this rifle does not have a half cock safety position nor a crossbold safety.
steps.quote: This firearm is designed with an ultra-safe patented Transfer Bar Safety Mechanism.
steps.cite: Henry H009B & Legacy H009 Series User Manual — undated — no edition, revision or form code is printed in the book — SAFETY, p.8

steps.title: Lever swung down and back to see what comes out
steps.action: Point the muzzle safely, swing the lever down and pull it back. If a cartridge ejects, the rifle was loaded and both the tube and the chamber need clearing. A tubular magazine shows nothing from outside, so this is the only way to find out what is in it.
steps.quote: Prior to loading your rifle, make certain that it is not already loaded. Point the muzzle in a safe direction, swing the lever down, and pull it back.
steps.cite: Henry H009B & Legacy H009 Series User Manual — undated — no edition, revision or form code is printed in the book — PRIOR TO LOADING YOUR HENRY .30/30 RIFLE, p.8

steps.title: Hammer down, inner magazine tube out, cartridges tipped clear
steps.action: With the hammer fully down, point the rifle up and withdraw the brass inner magazine tube — rotate it to disengage first. Tip the rifle downward and let the .30-30 cartridges slide out into a container, then replace the tube and cycle the lever to clear the chamber. Emptying the tube is not the same job as emptying the chamber, and this rifle needs both.
steps.quote: To unload the magazine and chamber, the hammer should be resting in the fired down position. With the rifle pointing upward, withdraw the inner magazine tube. Tip the gun downward, allowing cartridges to slide out into a container. Replace the inner magazine tube. Open the action again, by cycling the lever, to make certain that there are no cartridges in the chamber.
steps.cite: Henry H009B & Legacy H009 Series User Manual — undated — no edition, revision or form code is printed in the book — HOW TO UNLOAD THE MAGAZINE AND CHAMBER OF YOUR HENRY .30/30 RIFLE, p.9

steps.title: Action cycled repeatedly, then confirmed unloaded before solvent
steps.action: Work the lever several more times to be certain nothing is left on the carrier or in the chamber, and look at the chamber before you accept it. Henry restates the same requirement at the head of its maintenance section, which is a fair indication of how often it gets skipped.
steps.prose: Be sure that your gun is unloaded before attempting to clean.
steps.quote: Cycle the action multiple times to insure that no live rounds remain in the chamber.
steps.cite: Henry H009B & Legacy H009 Series User Manual — undated — no edition, revision or form code is printed in the book — HOW TO UNLOAD THE MAGAZINE AND CHAMBER OF YOUR HENRY .30/30 RIFLE, p.9

steps.title: Lever swung down to open the action
steps.action: Swing the lever down to open the action and hold it there. Henry is clear that this rifle does not need to be taken apart to be cleaned properly — assembled cleaning is the normal routine and the takedown in the Deep Clean branch is offered as a preference, not a requirement.
steps.quote: You do not have to disassemble this rifle in order to clean it sufficiently and to keep it operating properly.
steps.cite: Henry H009B & Legacy H009 Series User Manual — undated — no edition, revision or form code is printed in the book — HOW TO CLEAN YOUR HENRY .30/30 RIFLE, p.9

steps.title: Bore cleaned muzzle end toward the breech — as THIS book directs
steps.action: With the rifle assembled, this manual directs the rod down the bore from the muzzle end toward the breech. Take that seriously as written: it is what Henry prints for this rifle in this book, even though Henry's newer manuals for other models say the opposite. Because you are pushing fouling toward the action, wipe the chamber and breech out afterwards rather than leaving what the rod carried back there.
steps.caution: Once the rifle IS taken apart, the same manual switches direction and says to clean the bore from the breech end (p.10).
steps.quote: In order to clean it, we suggest that you first open the action by swinging the lever down. Use a brand name rifle cleaning kit and run the cleaning rod down the bore from the muzzle end toward the breech.
steps.cite: Henry H009B & Legacy H009 Series User Manual — undated — no edition, revision or form code is printed in the book — HOW TO CLEAN YOUR HENRY .30/30 RIFLE, p.9

steps.title: Bolt wiped and oiled
steps.action: Wipe the bolt clean of debris with solvent on a patch or small rag, then oil it. Get into the recess around the firing pin — .30-30 primers leave a hard carbon ring there that a dry rag will not shift. Oil lightly enough that it does not run back into the lockwork.
steps.quote: Wipe the bolt clean of any debris with solvent and a patch or small rag. Spray the bolt with some gun oil.
steps.cite: Henry H009B & Legacy H009 Series User Manual — undated — no edition, revision or form code is printed in the book — HOW TO CLEAN YOUR HENRY .30/30 RIFLE, p.9

steps.title: Every exposed metal surface left under a film of oil
steps.action: Wipe a film of oil over all exposed steel when you are done. Henry's phrasing is that rust is neglect. After damp weather wipe the bore and outside surfaces dry first and then re-oil — oiling over trapped moisture seals it against the steel instead of excluding it. Between seasons, re-oil the bore and metal parts and store the rifle somewhere dry.
steps.prose: Between seasons, periodically apply a coat of oil to the bore and metal parts and store in a dry place.
steps.quote: CLEANING WARNING: Remember - Rust is neglect - Make sure all exposed metal surfaces are coated with a film of oil.
steps.cite: Henry H009B & Legacy H009 Series User Manual — undated — no edition, revision or form code is printed in the book — MAINTENANCE, p.10

steps.title: Locking bolt: if it ever comes out, it goes back in
steps.action: If any work leaves the locking bolt out of the rifle, it must go back before the rifle is fired. Henry prints this in capitals on its own: the locking bolt is what keeps the breech closed against a .30-30 cartridge, so a rifle missing it is not a rifle with a fault, it is an open breech behind a full-power round.
steps.quote: WARNING: REMOVAL AND FAILURE TO RE-INSTALL THE LOCKING BOLT (PART 35) IS EXTREMELY DANGEROUS.
steps.cite: Henry H009B & Legacy H009 Series User Manual — undated — no edition, revision or form code is printed in the book — SIGHT ADJUSTMENTS, p.9

steps.title: Field strip complete
steps.action: That is Henry's assembled-rifle routine for the .30/30, and for most cleaning it is all that is wanted. This book is unusual in the Henry set in also printing a genuine takedown — lever screw, lever, bolt and ejector — and the Deep Clean branch follows it exactly, including the warning about the ejector coming loose.
steps.quote: You do not have to disassemble this rifle in order to clean it sufficiently and to keep it operating properly.
steps.cite: Henry H009B & Legacy H009 Series User Manual — undated — no edition, revision or form code is printed in the book — HOW TO CLEAN YOUR HENRY .30/30 RIFLE, p.9

deepSteps.title: Action open, lever screw out, lever off
deepSteps.action: Open the action by swinging the lever down, then take out the lever screw and lift the lever away. The screw is the lever's only attachment, and with the action open the lever is unloaded by the mainspring, which is why Henry has you open it first. Put the screw somewhere it cannot roll — it is small and it is the part that stops the rifle reassembling.
deepSteps.quote: If you prefer to take your rifle apart to clean it, then we suggest the following: Open the action by swinging the lever down. Remove the lever screw and then remove the lever.
deepSteps.cite: Henry H009B & Legacy H009 Series User Manual — undated — no edition, revision or form code is printed in the book — HOW TO CLEAN YOUR HENRY .30/30 RIFLE, p.10

deepSteps.title: Bolt out — and the ejector comes loose as it goes
deepSteps.action: Draw the bolt back out of the receiver. The moment it leaves, the ejector inside the receiver is no longer trapped, and Henry warns explicitly that it comes loose — this is the part that gets lost on this rifle. Work over a tray or a cloth and expect it to move as the bolt clears, rather than discovering it afterwards on the floor.
deepSteps.caution: This will loosen the ejector inside the receiver, so be very careful not to misplace it.
deepSteps.quote: Next, remove the bolt from the receiver. Note: This will loosen the ejector inside the receiver, so be very careful not to misplace it.
deepSteps.cite: Henry H009B & Legacy H009 Series User Manual — undated — no edition, revision or form code is printed in the book — HOW TO CLEAN YOUR HENRY .30/30 RIFLE, p.10

deepSteps.title: Ejector lifted out of its slot on the left side of the receiver
deepSteps.action: Take the ejector out of the slot in the left side wall of the receiver. Note which way round it sits before it comes out — it is a small flat part with an obvious orientation in the slot, and it has to go back the same way for the rifle to eject at all. Left side specifically: do not go looking for it on the right.
deepSteps.quote: You can then remove the ejector from the slot on the left side of the receiver.
deepSteps.cite: Henry H009B & Legacy H009 Series User Manual — undated — no edition, revision or form code is printed in the book — HOW TO CLEAN YOUR HENRY .30/30 RIFLE, p.10

deepSteps.title: Bore cleaned from the breech end with the rifle apart, bolt oiled, reverse to rebuild
deepSteps.action: With the bolt out you finally have a straight path in from the rear, and this is where the manual switches direction: clean the bore from the BREECH end now, following the bullet. Clean the bolt and oil it before it goes back. Reassembly is the reverse — ejector into its left-side slot first, then the bolt, then the lever and its screw.
deepSteps.quote: Use a brand name rifle cleaning kit and clean the bore from the breech end. Then clean the bolt and oil it before replacing. To reassemble, simply do the reverse.
deepSteps.cite: Henry H009B & Legacy H009 Series User Manual — undated — no edition, revision or form code is printed in the book — HOW TO CLEAN YOUR HENRY .30/30 RIFLE, p.10

deepSteps.title: After a soaking: Henry expects this teardown, not a wipe
deepSteps.action: If the rifle has been out in heavy rain, snow or salt spray, a wipe-down is not enough. Henry says a more thorough clean is needed and names what has to come off — the trigger guard and breech bolt assemblies — because water gets past the receiver openings and sits where a patch cannot reach. Salt spray in particular will not wait for the next range trip.
deepSteps.quote: If exposed to a soaking rain, snow or salt spray, a more thorough cleaning and oiling may be necessary, requiring removal of the trigger guard and breech bolt assemblies.
deepSteps.cite: Henry H009B & Legacy H009 Series User Manual — undated — no edition, revision or form code is printed in the book — MAINTENANCE, p.10

cleaning.name: BORE & CHAMBER
tasks: Assembled: run the rod from the muzzle end toward the breech, as this manual directs
Wipe the chamber and breech afterwards — that direction carries fouling back to them
Apart: clean the bore from the breech end instead, then dry and lightly oil

cleaning.name: BOLT & EJECTOR
tasks: Wipe carbon from the bolt face and the firing pin recess, then oil
If the bolt has been out, account for the ejector before anything else
Wipe the ejector and its left-side receiver slot clean and dry

cleaning.name: MAGAZINE TUBES & EXTERIOR
tasks: Wipe the brass inner magazine tube dry and check it is straight
Check the outer tube and loading port hold no stuck cartridge
Film of oil over all exposed steel; between seasons re-oil and store dry

reassembly: Set the ejector back into its slot on the left side of the receiver the way it came out.
Slide the bolt into the receiver, keeping the ejector in place as it passes.
Refit the lever and start the lever screw by hand before tightening it.
Reinstall the inner magazine tube and lock it into place.
To reassemble, simply do the reverse of the disassembly order.
fncheck: With the rifle confirmed empty, cycle the lever through full travel several times and confirm the action closes fully home, confirm the locking bolt is installed, and check that a dummy or empty case is ejected cleanly — a missing or reversed ejector shows up here and nowhere else.
